insider_note: Three facts: the process, two names, one organism. Lederberg and Tatum, in E. coli.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What conjugation is
steps.margin_note: Definition with 'direct contact' and the pilus. Three lines.
lines: CONJUGATION is the transfer of genetic material
between two bacterial cells through DIRECT
steps.why: Direct contact is what separates conjugation from the other two transfers: transformation needs no contact and transduction uses a virus.
common_mistakes: Saying conjugation needs a virus. That is TRANSDUCTION.
Leaving out 'direct contact'. It is what defines conjugation.
steps.memory_tip: Cell to cell, touching: that is conjugation.

steps.label: Who and where
steps.margin_note: Both names and the organism. Three lines.

lines.text: Lederberg and Tatum, in Escherichia coli

lines: It was discovered by LEDERBERG and TATUM.
steps.why: The same Lederberg also worked on transduction with Zinder, which is why the two discoveries are so easily confused.
common_mistakes: Naming Salmonella. That is the transduction organism; conjugation was in E. coli.
steps.memory_tip: Lederberg and Tatum in E. coli; Lederberg and Zinder in Salmonella.
